title: AHB Senior DV Recall Map
description: Open an interview anchor to rehearse the short answer, the deeper protocol reason, and the verification evidence a senior engineer should add.

signals.name: Who owns this phase?
signals.expansion: Address now, data from an earlier accepted address
signals.description: AHB pipelines address/control ahead of data. The data and response visible now belong to the previously accepted address phase, not necessarily the address currently on HADDR.
signals.sampled: Accepted edges where HREADY is HIGH
signals.verificationNote: Draw two adjacent cycles and label both owners before diagnosing any data mismatch.

signals.name: What freezes on a stall?
signals.expansion: Pending valid transfer and its data owner
signals.description: A valid pending address/control phase remains stable while HREADY is LOW, and stalled write data remains stable for its data phase.
signals.verificationNote: Mention IDLE, BUSY, and ERROR exceptions instead of claiming every signal is unconditionally frozen.

signals.name: Why two ERROR cycles?
signals.expansion: Stall the already-pipelined next address, then complete
signals.description: ERROR1 combines HRESP=1 with HREADY=0; ERROR2 keeps HRESP=1 and raises HREADY to finish the failed data phase.
signals.typicalUse: Explain optional cancellation of the following transfer
signals.verificationNote: Do not say the master must always abort the remainder; the specification permits cancellation or continuation.

signals.name: How do burst addresses work?
signals.expansion: HSIZE increment, HBURST count, wrap span, 1 KB rule
signals.description: The byte increment is 2^HSIZE. Fixed bursts contain 4, 8, or 16 beats; wrapping occurs within beats × bytes, and no incrementing burst crosses 1 KB.
signals.verificationNote: Calculate an example rather than reciting encodings; it reveals whether phase acceptance and BUSY handling are understood.

signals.name: Which AHB generation?
signals.expansion: Shared AHB, single-master AHB-Lite, optional AHB5
signals.description: Verification expectations change with the interface: original AHB includes shared-bus arbitration and legacy responses; AHB-Lite removes them; AHB5 adds declared optional capabilities.
signals.typicalUse: Avoid applying the wrong checker set
signals.verificationNote: Ask for the exact specification issue and configured properties before promising coverage or assertions.

signals.name: What proves verification?
signals.description: Protocol assertions catch cycle-level violations, scoreboards catch end-to-end corruption, coverage shows planned scenarios occurred, and debug artifacts explain failures and waivers.
signals.sampled: Across stable regressions and targeted closure
signals.typicalUse: Answer 'how did you know it was done?'
signals.verificationNote: A senior answer connects each risk to independent evidence instead of quoting one coverage percentage.
